groups.text: It is currently 17 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

The open-source community is pushing the limits of inference infrastructure with the release of vLLM version 0.26.0. This update arrived via 411 commits from 212 contributors, including 61 new developers. A primary addition is the Inkling model family, which now has a full support stack featuring LoRA and piecewise CUDA graph support. The release also targets DeepSeek-V4 performance across different vendors by introducing a specialized routing kernel and redundant repeat removal to lower latency. For those using AMD or XPU hardware, the update adds DSpark speculative decoding and a ROCm two-stage compressor for HCA prefill. Meanwhile, the Rust frontend has expanded its capabilities to include multimodal audio and video support. These technical shifts move toward more flexible attention backends and matured KV offloading, allowing developers to better manage secondary storage and CPU offloading for complex AI workloads.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is traveling to the United Kingdom this Monday for a high-stakes meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The central goal of the visit is for Zelensky to propose a formal drone agreement between the two nations. As part of this strategic partnership, London is expected to announce that it will share the intellectual property of a new British electronic jamming system with Ukraine. This move provides Kyiv with direct access to critical technology designed to neutralize aerial threats. By sharing these proprietary blueprints, the UK shifts from simply providing hardware to enabling Ukrainian technical autonomy in electronic warfare.

Berlin is reeling after a minibus was driven into crowds celebrating the Christopher Street Day festival. The attack left one person dead and dozens injured. Police have since shot and killed the primary suspect, a 21-year-old German man of Lebanese descent named Abdul B. Officers tracked him to an allotment garden in Berlin-Spandau, where he allegedly charged at them with a knife. According to the General Prosecutor's Office, authorities had already flagged Abdul B. as an Islamist threat who previously attempted to join the Islamic State in Syria. The Federal Prosecutor is now investigating whether he had accomplices. This event follows a pattern of vehicle-ramming attacks across Europe, North America, and China. In Germany alone, similar incidents occurred recently in Leipzig in May 2026 and Mannheim in March 2025, though investigators ruled out political motives in the Mannheim case.

In Berlin, a suspected Islamist terror attack on the Christopher Street Day parade has sparked sharp criticism of the German government. The Süddeutsche Zeitung reports that while officials expressed shock, their words ring hollow after the administration cut funding and treated queer policy as a secondary concern. Meanwhile, the Rheinzeitung warns that trust in state institutions is shrinking because known threats are falling through the cracks, noting that authorities are now searching for a man who would be imprisoned if his sentence had not been suspended. In Australia, far-right politician Pauline Hanson failed on Monday to overturn a racial vilification ruling. The court upheld that her 2022 demand for Senator Mehreen Faruqi to go back to Pakistan was a strong form of racism. Shifting to business, Paramount Skydance's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery is delayed until June 2027 after twelve U.S. states, led by California, blocked the merger.

Anthropic has launched Opus 5, a new AI model designed to balance high performance with lower costs. While Fable and Mythos now serve as the company's most powerful models, Opus 5 aims for near-parity with Fable 5 on certain tasks while costing half as much. Anthropic reports that Opus 5 achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves scientific research capabilities over the older Opus 4.8. In other news, farmers in Jamal, a village in India's Sirsa district, are relying on farm ponds called diggi to manage irrigation. These ponds allow them to mix low-cost canal water with groundwater, which is necessary because local groundwater often suffers from high salinity. Meanwhile, the football world is reflecting on what was likely Lionel Messi’s final World Cup. Spain defeated Argentina one-to-zero in the final at MetLife Stadium, denying the legendary captain a second consecutive title for the Albiceleste.

Developers using llama.cpp are seeing updates to how the server and user interface handle model names. The latest release fixes stream routes for models that contain a slash in their name, which previously caused issues when the decoded path split before capturing the conversation ID. To resolve this, the ID now moves to the query string on public routes and internal router hops where slashes survive encoding. This change ensures that stop and resume functions match the correct session. Additionally, the server now cancels pending requests if a stream is stopped while a model is still loading. Previously, a request could become an orphan because it was only registered after the blocking autoload wait. Now, conversations are registered before the wait, allowing a stop command to erase the entry and force the parked request to abort.

The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now topped 1,400 people. Health authorities report that confirmed infections have risen to 3,200 since the outbreak began in late April. The current fatality rate stands at 43.9 percent, though experts believe many cases remain undetected or unreported. Nearly 90 percent of these infections are concentrated in the northeastern province of Ituri, near the borders of South Sudan and Uganda. While scientists are racing to test vaccines against the rare Bundibugyo strain, the response has faced significant hurdles. Strikes by health workers over unpaid wages have hampered operations in some hospitals across the conflict-scarred east. The epidemic has already spread to five provinces, and experts warn that the crisis could continue for several more months.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 19 and 21 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays all day, followed by the BLISS Reading Group at six forty-five in the evening and Twerchhau at seven in the evening.
Mail worth checking: Operations Merantix Momentum sent your July payslip and tax certificate. Also, soerface updated a pull request regarding SEPA payment options.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
